candidate_relations.label: gynecomastia due to anabolic-steroid use
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly states that prior gynecomastia was already diagnosed and attributed to anabolic-steroid use (now discontinued). The current presentation is a NEW discrete 1-cm firm subareolar mass with lobular solid architecture on ultrasound and a lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography (BIRADS III), which is the basis for the reference diagnosis of intraductal papilloma. C001 names the prior resolved condition, not the new lesion, and gynecomastia is a diffuse glandular process incompatible with the discrete papillary intraductal neoplasm that is the reference answer.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Gynecomastia is a diffuse glandular enlargement; intraductal papilloma is a discrete benign intraductal neoplasm — different diagnostic entities within the same anatomical region

case_quality_flags: Prior gynecomastia history may create anchoring bias toward C001, but imaging clearly delineates a new discrete mass distinct from diffuse gynecomastia
